answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a refundable stake into shared escrow before it can trade, and rate-limit new entrants through a single inlet: only a few verified identities per day, each backed by a slowly earned reputation trail. Fake identities then cost real money and time, and a sudden flood of look-alike agents with velvet-smooth credentials stands out against the sparse, earned graph. Honest agents cluster in an oasis of mutually attested peers, so a newcomer must earn its way in through useful work rather than minting a thousand copies.
